title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 89
paragraphs: After this, Nicodromus, acting on his agreement with the Athenians, seized what is called the Old City. The Athenians, however, did not come to his support at the proper moment, for they did not happen to have enough ships to engage the Aeginetans. While they were busy asking the Corinthians to lend them ships, their whole plan fell to pieces. The Corinthians, who were then on very friendly terms with them, gave the Athenians twenty ships at their request, selling them for five drachmas apiece — since by their law they were not allowed to give them away for nothing. With these ships and their own, the Athenians sailed for Aegina with a total of seventy manned vessels, arriving one day later than the day agreed upon.
